problem: Prior VLN agents decide only over the local set of navigable neighbours at the current viewpoint. Error correction relies on one-step rollback (Regretful) or rule-based post-hoc search (beam, A*, FAST), which yields long trajectories and cannot be optimised jointly with the policy. Topological-memory methods need pre-exploration or offline graph sparsification, which does not suit online navigation in unseen environments. In addition, standard student-forcing supervision recomputes a shortest path to the goal, and that path can mismatch the instruction.
motivation: Following instructions in an unseen environment requires grounding language in a growing knowledge of the world and doing long-range planning, including exploration and backtracking over an ever-growing action space. The observation behind the paper is that an online-built graph of visited nodes plus unexplored action nodes lets any long-distance move, including a backtrack, become a single decision. Planning over such a graph can be kept cheap by working on a small instruction-conditioned pooled proxy graph instead of the full graph.
key_idea: Build a graph online whose internal nodes are visited locations and whose leaves are all unexplored actions, then choose the next action globally over every leaf via GNN message passing on learned, attention-pooled multi-channel proxy graphs, trained purely by imitation with graph-augmented 'correction' supervision.
insight: Enlarging the decision space to the global graph is what drives the gains. In the Table 3 ablation on R2R val-unseen, lowering top-K leaf expansion from 16 to 10/5/3 steadily drops SR from 52 to 50/49/47. Message passing on the proxy graph matters: SR goes from 42 (mp=0) to 50 (mp=3, 1 channel), and 3 independent channels reach 52. A single channel with 3× graph dimension gives only 49, so the channel gain is not about parameter count. Graph-augmented supervision, which picks the node on the GT path that maximises path similarity to the expert, beats shortest-path student-forcing supervision (SR 52 vs 46, SPL 41 vs 36). This supervision is also what allows pure-IL training to work on R4R, where instruction fidelity matters.
method: Base agent: the co-grounding Self-Monitoring agent without the progress-monitor auxiliary loss. It has an LSTM instruction encoder and an attention-based LSTM decoder over pre-computed panoramic ResNet features; the hidden state h_t is updated at every executed step.

Evolving graph: grows online. Internal nodes embed visited locations (from o_t) and leaf nodes embed candidate navigable actions (from o_a); the two use separate networks. A connectivity tensor M_t has 3 edge function types: forward and backward between visited nodes, and visited→leaf. Only the top-K leaves by policy confidence are added (default K=16, i.e. all).

Global action space with graph jump: the policy scores every leaf node in the graph. For a chosen, possibly distant, leaf the agent computes a shortest-path route on its own graph and executes it in one decision, so backtracking or error correction takes a single step. h_t keeps updating along the internal route.

Proxy-graph pooling: a lightweight GNN_L conditioned on [h_t; c] outputs a softmax assignment A_t (DiffPool-style normalized pooling). This produces a fixed-size proxy graph: V̄=AᵀV, M̄_i=AᵀM_iA per function type, Ē_i=AᵀE_iA per edge dimension.

Planning core: GNN_P runs K_P=3 message-passing steps with typed messages, context-conditioned input nets and graph dim 256 on the proxy graph. Refined nodes are unpooled back to the full graph, and action logits come from a dot product (W_hv h_t)ᵀ v_i with a softmax over all leaves. Multi-channel planning uses several independent proxy graphs (default 3) whose outputs are summed.

Graph-augmented supervision for student forcing: at each step the label is the node on the GT route τ* that maximises a path-similarity metric M(τ_t ∪ v, τ*). Such nodes are guaranteed to be in the graph. This replaces recomputed shortest-path-to-goal labels. Training uses cross-entropy only (pure IL), Adam, lr 1e-4.

setting.backbone: LSTM instruction encoder + attention LSTM decoder (Self-Monitoring co-grounding agent) + GNN pooling/planning modules, on frozen pre-computed ResNet panoramic features; trained from scratch with imitation learning
setting.training_data: R2R train (14,039 instructions). EGP* additionally uses 178,330 Speaker-Follower synthetic instruction-route pairs. R4R model trained on R4R train (233,532 instructions). Pure imitation learning, no RL.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (pre-computed ResNet features per view) + candidate navigable-location features
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints, generalized to a global action space: select any unexplored leaf node in the agent-built graph, reached via shortest-path 'graph jump' over already-visited nodes
setting.privileged: none beyond the standard R2R nav-graph connectivity (navigable locations) provided by the simulator; graph jumps are planned on the agent's own online-built graph

results: On R2R, EGP without augmentation lifts the baseline co-grounding agent on val-unseen from SR 43 to 52 and SPL 36 to 41 (NE 6.20→5.34). With Speaker augmentation, EGP* reaches 56 SR / 44 SPL on val-unseen and 53 SR / 42 SPL / 5.34 NE on test, beating the strongest architecture baseline, Regretful* (48 SR / 40 SPL on test), by 5 SR. On R4R val-unseen, EGP is trained with pure IL yet beats IL+RL baselines (RCM fidelity-oriented, PTA). It reaches CLS 44.4, nDTW 37.4 and SDTW 17.5, which is +7.0 CLS, +5.0 nDTW and +4.9 SDTW over the best prior, with a moderate path length of 18.3.
limitations: Evaluated only on the discrete Matterport3D nav-graph (R2R/R4R). Graph jump assumes free multi-hop traversal over known connectivity, so it does not transfer directly to continuous or real-robot settings.

The graph grows with the episode. The proxy graph caps planning cost, but the full graph is still stored and pooled at each step; the authors note that computation and planning time-scale remain open issues.
Uses older ResNet features and an LSTM backbone with pure IL, and does not combine with pre-training (e.g. PREVALENT) or RL. R4R is reported only on val-unseen, and val-seen results are absent.
